name: Rolled Short Put Repair
summary: A management pattern rather than an entry: roll a losing short put down and out for a net credit to buy time and lower the strike, with a hard limit on how many times.

legs.strike_rule: Buy to close the existing tested short put
Sell a new put at a strike 3-8% lower, targeting delta -0.25 to -0.30
legs.dte_rule: 30-45 DTE from the roll date, always further out than the original

max_profit: The new credit plus all credits previously collected on the position
max_loss: (new strike - cumulative credits) x 100. Max loss FALLS with each credit-positive roll, but duration and capital lock-up both extend.
breakevens: new strike - cumulative credits collected across all rolls

greeks.delta: reset to +0.25 to +0.30 after the roll
greeks.gamma: reset lower by moving further out in time

when_to_use: When a short put's delta exceeds -0.50 but the underlying thesis is intact and the roll can be done for a net credit. Never use it to avoid taking a loss on a broken thesis.
entry_rules: Trigger: existing short put delta exceeds -0.50, OR the underlying has fallen more than 1.5 ATR since entry
The roll MUST be executed for a net credit. If no credit is available at a lower strike and later expiry, do not roll - close the position and take the loss
New strike at least 3% below the old strike
New expiry at least 21 days beyond the current one, and 30-45 DTE total
Roll counter: maximum 2 rolls per original position. On the third trigger, close
Hard abort: if the underlying has fallen more than 20% from the original entry, or has broken its 200-day SMA on a weekly closing basis, close rather than roll
Submit as a single multi-leg roll order to avoid legging risk, never as two separate orders
management_rules: After the roll, manage the new position with standard CSP rules: close at 50% of the NEW credit, or at 21 DTE
Track cumulative credit and cumulative days-in-trade per original position; if days-in-trade exceeds 120, close regardless
Never increase contract count on a roll. Rolling into more contracts to make it back converts a manageable loss into an account event
Capital check: the rolled position still ties up new_strike x 100 in cash. Confirm it does not breach the 20%-of-equity per-position limit
exit_rules: Close at 50% of the new credit, at 21 DTE, at the 2-roll limit, or on the 20%-decline / 200-day-SMA abort
NEVER-ASSIGN RULE persists across rolls: extrinsic < $0.10, delta > -0.85, within 1.0% of the strike at 14:30 ET on expiry day, hard backstop 15:45 ET
The roll itself must be completed before the never-assign timer on the OLD position fires. Schedule rolls no later than 3 DTE on the original contract
assignment_risk: The roll's buy-to-close leg removes the old contract's assignment risk instantly; the new short put carries fresh, lower assignment risk. The danger is a partial fill that closes nothing and opens a second short put - always submit as a single net order and verify both legs filled.
buying_power: New strike x 100 in cash. Slightly less than before if rolled down.
liquidity_needs: Rolling requires a liquid chain at BOTH strikes and BOTH expiries. If the target strike has OI < 250, the roll is not viable - close instead.
common_mistakes: Rolling for a debit and calling it management; rolling indefinitely and turning a 2-week trade into a 9-month hostage position; rolling into a bigger contract count; legging the roll and being momentarily short two puts.
zero_dte_notes: Rolling is not possible at 0 DTE - there is no later same-day expiry. 0DTE positions are closed, never rolled.
